Reclassified from Medium to intended-design via /review-finding.

findings.triageReason: Intended design (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m3). emergencyWithdraw/withdraw/deposit are deliberately frozen once migrationInfo[token].active because initiateMigration captures an immutable (R,P) snapshot and every exit pays a fixed pro-rata credit p_i*min(R,P)/P; a live exit during migration would mutate P and corrupt the snapshot (StableStaker.sol:306-307, 335-340). The Law-2 'faithfulness gap' framing is therefore invalid. The residual 'revoke staker's phUSD minter while migration active -> exits revert' sliver is an obvious admin misstep (Law 3 out-of-scope) and recoverable. Not submittable.

findings.description: During an active terminal migration, emergencyWithdraw is blocked (migration active), and the only exits (userMigrate, batchMigrate) mint frozen pending phUSD via _exitPosition -> phUSD.mint BEFORE transferring principal. If the staker loses phUSD minter rights while a token is active, those exits revert on the pending-phUSD mint and principal is retrievable only after minter rights are restored. Healthy mode has a mint-free escape (emergencyWithdraw); terminal mode does not. Bounded by the owner-trusted precondition 'minter revoked mid-migration'.

findings.title: Idle-pool strategy adoption discards creditedPrincipal, shorting last withdrawers

Adopting a haircutting (market) strategy over a non-empty idle pool leaves poolInfo.totalStaked at full nominal value while strategy.principalOf(this) = idleBalance * (1 - slip), producing a silent last-withdrawer FCFS shortfall on the healthy-withdraw path; the underwater guard is blind because it compares strategy-internal totalBalanceOf vs principalOf. findings.summary: _routeExit returns only the strategy-withdrawal delta (t.balanceOf(this) - balanceBefore, :801-803), so the staker's pre-existing idle set-aside buffer never enters R. Credits are amt * min(R,P) / P (:536-537), so the buffer can never reduce a haircut. initiateMigration:472-475 states the choice explicitly ('Surplus is NOT swept ... stays inside the now-decoupled strategy as protocol-owned value and never reaches users'). When a strategy is underwater, R < P and every user takes a proportional haircut while the liquid cushion sits unused. Live at block 25,851,231: USDe 48.506672 (2.35% of that pool's principal), USDC 9.941647 (0.49%), DOLA 6.663469 (0.54%).
findings.citationNote: The correct citation is src/StableStaker.sol:472-475. An earlier draft cited :471, which is a blank line.

authority.basis: Law 2 (faithfulness). This finding does not exist without the owner's stated intent: the code is internally consistent and does exactly what its own comment at :472-475 says.
authority.ownerQuote: I want all yield and setAside buffer swept into principal during a migration... I'm not as interested in precise migrations as I am in safe migrations erring on the side of the user if possible, but never wrecking the protocol in a way that breaks any functionality (exploit vector).
authority.conflict: The current behaviour errs AGAINST the user, the opposite of the owner's stated priority.

recommendation.fix: Include the staker's pre-existing idle balance for the token in R (sample t.balanceOf(address(this)) BEFORE _routeExit runs, since _routeExit transfers proceeds into the same balance).
recommendation.safeByConstruction: Credits are already capped at min(R,P) (:536-537), so a larger R can only REDUCE a haircut and can never over-credit. The comment at :474-475 already relies on that same cap to defend against a donation-inflated R.
recommendation.noLiquidityImplication: PURE ACCOUNTING CHANGE. Credits are already paid by plain safeTransfer from the staker's whole balance (:571), so the buffer is ALREADY spendable for credits - it is only never counted.

severityNote.mediumCounterArgument: Recorded honestly rather than buried: the USDe buffer is 2.35% of pool principal, so a ~2% impairment would be almost entirely absorbable and users would be haircut anyway.
severityNote.whyLowStands: No C4 Medium prong is met - no value is lost (it stays protocol-owned) and migration still functions.
severityNote.ownersCall: If the owner reads 'users haircut while the designated cushion sits idle' as a functional failure, Medium is defensible. This is the owner's call, not the auditor's.
